topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture’s place in the cancer course and states what students should learn about cancer causation.

topics.label: Mutations and susceptibility in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations lead to cancer through clonal evolution within a susceptible cellular and microenvironmental context.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk and how that contribution can be distinguished from chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection can drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and cancer-promoting conditions.

topics.label: How environmental carcinogens damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular processes through which environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from the promotion that enables initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Carcinogen susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the explanation of context-dependent carcinogenesis by examining developmental susceptibility and recapping the mechanisms established earlier.

topics.label: Tracing carcinogenic exposures in human populations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence obtained from people can link carcinogen exposure to cancer without deliberately exposing them.

topics.label: Experimental tests of carcinogenicity and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate controlled experimental tests for carcinogenic potential and explain why their results may not fully predict human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture’s conclusions about environmental cancer risk and places them within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
